name: Museum of Contemporary Art Yinchuan
funding: Founded 2012-15 by Ningxia Minsheng Real Estate (property developer) with the provincial government under a BOT deal; about 300m yuan build.
records_note: The museum's website could not be opened, so its reports, accounts, funders and board stay unchecked.

name: Museum of Free Belarus
funding: Project of the National Anti-Crisis Management (Pavel Latushka); 367 m2 premises at Foksal 11 provided by the City of Warsaw; Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage, Culture Support Fund (Digital Culture 2025 co-financing); individual donors via PayPal and crypto; Fundacja Białoruś Przyszłości
watch: Opened 17 Jul 2022 with Polish government backing; about 700 artefacts of the 2020 protest movement plus digital testimonies; cooperation agreements with Poland's National Institute of Museology, the Karta Foundation and the Hoover Institution; nominated for EMYA 2027 and longlisted for the Council of Europe Museum Prize; in July 2026 it says it is still seeking a permanent home.
records_note: A project of the National Anti-Crisis Management: no reports, accounts or funder list; the parent names its leadership and takes PayPal and crypto donations.

name: Museum of Jurassic Technology
funding: Expenses $0.6M (FY2023); members, founder David Wilson, Getty and Mike Kelley Foundation grants 2024, LA city and county arts funds.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies is on the only published foundation roster. The page's footer says 1996-2001, but that name dates the list after 2006. No current roster is published.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, one undated page names foundation funders, and no board is listed.

name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sri Lanka
funding: Non-profit set up in 2019, with no fixed venue. Founding Patrons are individuals; the John Keells Foundation was named primary sponsor in March 2020.
watch: John Keells Holdings, the foundation's parent, developed the City of Dreams Sri Lanka resort (opened August 2025); Melco manages the casino with JKH.
records_note: It posts its 2025/26 audit report, names its board, and lists Founding Patrons for 2026; no earlier annual reports are linked.

name: Museum of Modern Egyptian Art
watch: Holds more than 13,000 works. Ahram Online reported a partial closure; no removed or censored works are documented.
records_note: No official site was found; searches returned only third-party pages, so no reports, accounts, funder list or board are published that we could find.

name: Museum of Russian Impressionism
funding: Private: founded by Boris Mints (O1 Group) in 2016; since Feb 2024 the patron-trustee is Vladimir Voronin, shareholder of property developer FSK Group (property money, allowed).
watch: Mints left Russia and could no longer support the museum; Voronin began funding exhibitions in 2023 and took over as permanent trustee on 15 Feb 2024. OpenSanctions lists Mints only in an oligarch/Wikidata database, not on any sanctions list.
records_note: The museum's own site would not load from here, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; only press coverage was readable.

name: Museum Tinguely
funding: Roche has paid all operating costs since the museum opened in 1996 as a gift for its centenary; Roche built it and funds collection additions.
watch: Roche pleaded guilty in 1999 to a worldwide vitamin price-fixing conspiracy and paid $500M in US criminal fines.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; funder Roche posts annual and finance reports 2020 to 2025 and its board; no donor list.

name: Musée d'art de Joliette
funding: Quebec ministries, Canada Council and Ville de Joliette. Énergir, Power Corporation, Fondation Hydro-Québec, Caisse Desjardins and the Lassonde and DeSève foundations are among its lead partners (2025 annual report).
watch: Énergir (natural-gas utility) and Fondation Famille Pierre Lassonde (mining fortune) on current partners list; Power Corp funds a named room.
records_note: It posts nine annual reports from 2016-17 to 2024-25 with audited statements, names its board and lists partners and donors.

name: Musée des Civilisations Noires
funding: Senegalese state museum. China financed the building with a CFA 20 billion (over EUR 30M) grant. 2025 own revenue was CFA 353.9M.
watch: China's grant paid for the building, not operations.
records_note: Its site did not open from here; a search listing shows a 2025 activity report, and nothing on accounts, funders or board was checked.

name: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec
funding: C$34.1M revenue 2023-24 (C$24.5M Quebec grants), 248,643 visitors; sponsors Hydro-Québec, Simons, Air Canada, Banque Nationale, BMO, Desjardins, RBC Foundation.
watch: Donor wall lists Imperial Oil ($500k+ cumulative, not in 2023-24 list), Rio Tinto, Osisko, SNC-Lavalin and Loto-Québec. Also the Lassonde (mining) pavilion gift.
records_note: Posts its 2023-24 and 2024-25 annual reports with audited statements, a named donor list for the 2025-26 campaign, and its board in the reports.

name: MUU Helsinki Contemporary Art Centre
funding: Arts Promotion Centre Finland (Taike), City of Helsinki, Finnish Cultural Foundation; non-profit artists' association.
watch: Founded in 1987 by artists; promotes experimental and non-traditional art forms, sound art, performance, and video art.

name: Muzeum Sztuki in Łódź (ms1 & ms2)
funding: Public museum funded by the city and the Ministry of Culture.
watch: No ORLEN, PGE or Azoty link found.
records_note: Posts activity reports for 2016 to 2025, profit and loss accounts for 2016 to 2023 and its 15-member museum council; no named funder list.
